utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I see that our next witness is in court. Good morning, sir. Would you please stand and would you please read aloud the affirmation on this card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Shin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could remind you to speak up slightly when giving your answers during these proceedings. Witness, I'd like to begin by reminding you that you have been granted protective measures in this case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These protective measures include the following: You have been granted a pseudonym, which will be used in place of your real name during these proceedings; you have also been granted image distortion which means that outside of this Tribunal your face will be disguised; in addition, you have also been granted voice distortion. What that means is that outside of this Tribunal your voice will also be disguised. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would ask you during the course of your testimony not to use your own name or the name of your village. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would remind you also that there will be times during your testimony when we will be going into private session. I will be indicating to you when we are in private session and when we are in open session and at the moment we are in open session. I'm sorry, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you, with the assistance of the usher, a piece of paper. If you could please look at that paper and read it to yourself not out loud and just indicate whether that is your true name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that sheet could be given an exhibit number and placed under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we could show that to Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, during these proceedings I will be referring to you as either -- under your pseudonym, Shefqet Kabashi, or simply as "Witness." Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could please just be told what exhibit number that sheet is given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're waiting for the system to come up, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P162, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honours, if we could go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session. 11 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, we are now in private session and I'll be asking you a few questions about your background while we are in private session. Could you please tell the Court your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The 1st of July, 1976.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which -- where were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I was born in Zahac village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which municipality is that village in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Peja municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you are by ethnicity a Kosovar Albanian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what is your current profession?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I work in the Kosova police corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe just briefly what your functions are in the Kosovo police corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: We take care of protecting measures for the government facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how long have you been in the Kosovo police corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: About five months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No. We expect one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I've been asked if you can please just speak up a little more loudly when giving your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are now back in open session, and I would remind you that you do have protective measures in these proceedings, including the image distortion that we spoke of earlier as well as the voice distortion. So while we are in open session please, as I mentioned before, do not mention your name or the name of your village. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall that you gave two statements to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor in October and in December of 2004?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give those statements voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. After the Prosecutors asked me to give a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from some corrections and explanations which we had discussed earlier this week, were you as truthful as you could be in those statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to direct you now to 1998. Were you at some point in 1998 a member of the KLA? And if you could just indicate yes or no at this point, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the KLA to -- as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I joined the KLA in April 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you can recall, do you remember when in April of 1998 you joined? Was it in the early, the middle, or the later part of that month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I think it was the 9th of April or a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where it was, the name of the place, that you went to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, I understand the defendants cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have to hope that the volume controls on their mechanism can cope with that and the usher will attend to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's not clear to me whether it's a fault in the system or a problem with the witness's speech volume. But can I say this to you, sir, it would help both the interpreters and everybody else if you were able to speak more loudly. I know this is a strange surrounding, but I hope you will be able to settle down and remember to speak in a more ordinary tone. At the moment your words hardly can be heard by anybody in this courtroom. So if you could just speak in a more loud tone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm told the defendants can hear you, therefore if they can hear you I would assume there's nothing wrong with their headsets. It may have been the witness needed to move closer to the microphone for them to hear him more clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. We will proceed and see whether there's any improvement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as you've seen, some steps have been taken to assist with the volume here, but if you could speak up just a little bit more. There is also a glass of water near you if you need any water at any point. Returning to where we left off, I was asking you if you could please tell the Court, if you could please tell the Judges, what -- where you went to join the KLA, the name of the place when you went in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went to Jablanice village, Djakova municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I will now show you a map, and it's I believe it's a map I've shown you before. It's a map of west Kosovo. Now, Witness, the map has been placed on that machine that, as you can see, but if you can try and see if you can locate -- I know the writing is a little bit small on that map, but if you can try and locate Jablanica village. And please take your time, if you can just indicate when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if the usher could provide a pointer first to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could point out when you've found the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is where the village is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If the usher could provide a red pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you circle with that red pen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that map could please be given an exhibit number and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P163, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. We seem to be having various types of technical difficulties this morning, but I hope that's okay now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, reminding you that we are in open session right now, could you indicate whether when you went to Jablanica village you went alone or you went with somebody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went with my cousin, the son of my uncle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why -- Witness, why did you join the KLA? If you could explain your reasons, your motivation at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Because it was a very hard time for us in Kosova, I mean us Albanians. The violence was excessive against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you who was perpetrating that violence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself have any specific problems in connection with this violence being perpetrated against the Kosovar Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that the Judges can understand, could you explain one of those incidents, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: To my recollection it was in 1991. The Serbs came to check our homes and beat us until 1995. This went on continuously. In 1996 I started working; I still had problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, were there any problems that you had of this type in 1998 before you joined the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: That was the last incident that occurred before I joined the KLA. We had a bar in the city. I worked there with some of my relatives. A policeman came. We knew him as policeman. He was not in uniform. He cursed us. He said that, We will drive you away from here. This is not a place for you. You should close this place. My uncle came; he was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. close by. And he asked, What is the problem? The Serb policeman gave him a blow and threatened to take him to the police station. My uncle tried to stop him. He tried to pull out his pistol to kill my uncle. Then I intervened and the son of my uncle was behind me, and we took away his pistol. Unfortunately, the police station was very close by and many policemen came and arrested us and took us to the police station. It was evening when this happened, and the war was taking place in Drenica. They got some information that there is a fighting going on and only three policemen remained at the station. They released us and told us that they were going to take us back tomorrow. I didn't go to work after that. It was a time of the protests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just interrupt you there to ask you a couple of questions about that. As far as you know, was there -- was there any reason for the policeman to come to you -- to your place of work at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. The reason was that we were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was -- what was the -- when did this incident occur in relation to the time that you went to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: This may have happened at the end of March or the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, just that we're clear, that's in 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you were going to join the KLA in April of 1998, what did you believe the KLA stood for? What ideals did you believe they stood for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I joined the KLA because I wanted to fight for the -- for my people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you the next set of questions, and reminding you that we are in open session. Could you please explain to the Court how you knew that Jablanica was a place where you could join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I knew that because a village close to Jablanica but also in Jablanica itself, in those village I have relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to Jablanica village, could you please tell us where you first went, where in particular.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went to the house of one of my relatives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before we continue with that, I should have asked you this a minute ago, when you told us that you knew people in Jablanica and close -- in a village close to Jablanica, what did you mean by that? Did they tell you something about the KLA and the possibility of joining there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I had heard even before, but I wasn't sure. So one night before the day that I actually joined I went there. They stopped me at the entrance to the village. They asked me who I was, where I was coming from. Those people were in uniforms. I asked them if they accepted new soldiers; they said, Yes, but you have to go to the staff first. I returned home that night and I went back tomorrow with my uncle -- with the son of my uncle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your last answer the translation is that the soldiers told you you have to go to the staff. Is that the proper word, "staff"? I'm not sure if the translation was correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, the soldiers that stopped me told me that, If you are interested, you have to go to the staff, meaning the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So did you then go to the headquarters or did you do something else first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: That night I went back home and I went back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went to this relative of mine - and I don't like to mention the names of the people I met there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, don't mention the names of your relatives since we are in open session, but otherwise please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know what you want me to say for the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's my error. I will try to be more clear. So after you went to this relative of yours, did you then -- did you then go to the headquarters or did you meet anyone from the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, I met someone else, someone who asked me whether I wanted to go to Albania to get arms. I said, Yes, this is why I'm here for. And that night we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could just interrupt you briefly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. 24 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are now in private session. We'll just be in private session very briefly. Could you mention the name of that person who told you about the possibility of going to Albania to get weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, Hajdar Dula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you understood at that time, did you know what his position was or did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: For that time to me he appeared to be just a simple KLA soldier. I didn't know his position. We met in the house of my relative; that's where we discussed this. And in the evening we set off for Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could go back into open, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we do, a little earlier you mentioned the village where this occurred and there are relatives of the witness in that village. Should the name of the village be redacted?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe there's a need to redact the name of the village, but if we could please redact the phrase "relative" or "relative of mine."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before we go into open session I would just inform you that your reference to relatives in the village of Jablanica will be redacted, which means that it will not appear in any public transcript nor will it be heard in the transmission of this proceeding outside of the courtroom. Do you understand that? And likewise, if in the future when referring to these relatives, if you could please refer to "people that you know" in that village rather than "relatives," I think we would be able to save a step in the redaction process.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we'll be able to provide a more specific reference to that at the first break. If we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll go to public session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were telling us that someone had come to ask you whether you would be able to go to Albania that evening. Did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Did you then in fact set off for Albania? Just yes or no please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who you went to Albania with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: With my cousin and many others. There were two persons who usually escorted the others through the way. One comes from that village and the other from a village nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that there were many others, were these others -- who were these others? Were they soldiers of the KLA? Were they other civilians? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: There were soldiers as well, but they were more or less of the same position like mine. There were people who wanted to join the KLA and take up arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately, as far as you can recall, how many people were there in this group that went to Albania?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the exact number, but I know they were in hundreds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for at least some of these people, did you know whether this was their first time to Albania or whether -- whether they had been there before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I mentioned earlier that there were many just like me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were there people within that group who knew the way, who knew how to go there, how to go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned it earlier. One of them was from that village and the other from another village who travelled frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you mentioned that earlier you had told us that you usually escorted the others through the way. Would it be correct that that means they had been to Albania previously? Just to be clear. It may perhaps be obvious.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you knew at that time, had they -- the previous times that these people, these two people you mentioned, had been there, had they also been there for the purpose of gathering or acquiring weapons for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No. I knew them just as people who escorted us. I don't know what their tasks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could go briefly into private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. 2 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are now in private session. Could you please tell us the names of those people who had, as you described, this escorting function.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Fadil Nimani and Agim Zeneli.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can go into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're now back in open session and I would just ask you, did you in fact arrive in Albania and gather or acquire weapons there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. We travelled that night, and the next day sometime in the morning we arrived there. I don't know who collected the weapons, but we did take heavy weaponry, ammunition, cannons, shells, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I forgot to ask you, on your way towards Albania with this group, did you encounter any similar groups coming back the same path?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, we met.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this group or groups that you met, were they also returning with weapons to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you -- after your group had taken this weapon -- taken these weapons, including this heavy weaponry, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: We returned to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you bring the weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: To the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that point after you had returned with the weaponry, were you -- were you then accepted into the KLA or registered in the KLA, or did something else happen? If you could just say yes or no first, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, I wasn't accepted right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain then what happened next. Again, I remind you that we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went back to these people that I knew. We had some rest. In other words, we arrived sometime in the morning. We rested for that day. And I'm not quite sure whether it was on that evening or the next weekend that the person whom I mentioned earlier came and asked me whether I was willing to go to the front. I said yes. He gave me his weapon, a uniform, and his vehicle. And together with my cousin, we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you then go to the front and engage in combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: There was firing, there was shelling in Cermjan, the place where this took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Cermjan, that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Till the next day, sometime around 10.00 or 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that point, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: An officer that we had, he asked for volunteers to attack the Serb positions at Cuka i Vogel. 15 of us went. There was a combat for half an hour and then we returned back to our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you returned to your positions, do you -- does that mean that you returned -- let me put it this way: When you say you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. returned to your positions, where were it that you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I referred to the positions at Cuka e Crmjanit. In other words, it was the front line that was held by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long were you at this front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: We went there a night before and stayed there till 10.00 the next morning. We were there during that attack and then returned back to Jablanice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you returned back to Jablanica, were you at that point accepted into the KLA or registered with the KLA or did something else happen first? If we could -- if you could just say yes or no please first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Something else happened and I was not accepted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Judges what happened next.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went to this person that I knew. My cousin was returned home in order to find out if there was something new. I waited, maybe for a day, two or three, and then went to the staff, to the headquarters. I addressed the leader of that headquarters, in fact it was his house. I said to him, I came here to join and become a soldier. He said that there was lack of weapons, but I insisted to join. He went inside. He gave me a weapon, a sniper rifle, a very old Russian made. And with his vehicle he took me to the barracks which was -- which were situated in a house in the end part of the village. It was a place where soldiers were staying. He handed me over to another leader. He told him my name. He asked me if I had a pseudonym. I said, No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry, I would remind you at that point not to mention the pseudonym while we're in open session. I'm sorry to interrupt you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I told him I didn't have a pseudonym and explained that from my childhood I was called by a certain name and that's what they used then as a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, how much time had passed at this point between the time that you had first gone to Jablanica to join the KLA and the time now when you were given this weapon and brought over to these barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It could be a week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is your -- what is your understanding about why it is that there was this -- there was this difference of one week and why it was that you were not accepted into the KLA at the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I thought that the army was highly professional, and for this reason I had to check people that it accepted in its ranks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: They had to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you to the interpreters for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you say that they had to check people that they accepted into its ranks, what was your understanding about what they were checking for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I will again repeat here that this is my opinion that they had to check the background, which family they came from, if they were collaborators with the enemy, our enemy at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "collaborators with the enemy," just to be clear could you please indicate who that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The Serbs were our enemy, and collaborator was someone who cooperated with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry some of the questions are a little obvious, but I have to ask them anyway. When you say that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that your -- you thought that the -- the KLA was highly professional and for that reason they had to check people before accepting them into their ranks, just to be clear is that because your belief, your understanding, was that a professional army would undertake that kind of check?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's that time again. The question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness's understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it has two problems. One is the question is leading; second is that there is a lack of foundation with regard to the issue of a "professional army." In the absence of a foundation, there's no information that this witness is competent to testify with regard to that particular issue, which I think is of some importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, thank you. Mr. Shin, is there anything you wish to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I'll just move on actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. That will make Mr. Guy-Smith very happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm happy to make Mr. Guy-Smith happy. For the next few questions, Your Honour -- for the next few questions, Your Honour, if we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. 5 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are now in private session and I'll just ask you a few questions about the names of some of the people you've mentioned. You said that the KLA -- that the headquarters was also someone's house. Could you please tell us whose house that was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was the house of Lahi Ibrahimaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mention also that this man, Lahi Ibrahimaj, had handed you over to someone else at the barracks. Could you please tell us the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. His name was Afrim. I don't know his family name. His pseudonym was Leopard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, while we are in private session I would ask you, you indicated that you were asked to provide this nickname that you were known since -- known by since childhood. Would you please tell the Judges what that name was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Shullc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We can return to open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we are now back in open session and I'd like to ask you now, were you -- actually, could I ask you this first: When you were brought to the barracks was there -- did you give your name to anybody or how was the actual registration process? How did that take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I gave them my name and pseudonym that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that -- when you say you gave them your name, did you write it down anywhere or what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, I didn't, but he did write it down. And he wrote my pseudonym as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "he wrote it down," without mentioning a name could you just describe which person it was who wrote that down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The person who accepted me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm sorry this is a little bit awkward because we are in open session, but when you say accepted you "there," do you mean the barracks or do you mean the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. After this did you receive training of any sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From time -- when you say "from time to time," could you explain or could you tell us the time period within which this training occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The training occurred sometime in mid-May after I had started to participate in other fronts as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you describe briefly the kind of training that was provided to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Running, crawling exercises with weapons, and other. Weapons, different types of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us also, please, where it was that you received this training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: In that village and in the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "in that village," that means the village where you joined the KLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to take you now to the time period in May 1998 somewhere around the 19th to the 21st of May. Do you recall where you were and what you were doing during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Kpuz village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you at some point go somewhere from Kpuz village during that time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went to Qeskove village. There was front there as well. In Bokshiq village, too, and Grabanica village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you went there to that front, did you engage in combat, in those locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you alone when you went there or did you go with other people, other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: We were several friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us first, these villages that you mentioned, Bokshiq, Grabanica, and this other village, how close are they to each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: They are as if joined together. They are like on the border with each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you went to the front there, just to be clear, that was -- that was a single front line there or were there more than one front lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: There were several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how long you spent on the front lines in that area at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: On the 20th of May in the evening I stayed in Bokshiq. There was shelling from both sides, both from the Serbian side and our side. The following day, on the 21st at around 10.00 we left and stayed until 5.00 in the afternoon, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that combat there, do you know whether the -- the enemy forces suffered any casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I heard that there were casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about your side, the KLA side, did you suffer any casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, there were. A friend of mine was killed and there were injured as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of this combat or shortly afterwards, do you know what happened to the people from Grabanica village? Did they stay there or did they go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, they fled. They fled the shelling and went to the village of Glodjane and to other villages as well where they could find shelter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether -- whether the KLA went to speak, whether anyone from the KLA went to speak to -- went to speak to the villagers from Grabanica when they were in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I just heard about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- before you tell us what you heard, could you tell us to the best of your recollection who you heard this from. You don't need to mention a name, but if you could try to describe that person or persons for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I heard this from those who I knew. I knew many persons from that region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do I understand from your answer that you heard this from more than one person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us then what it is you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The leaders asked them, Why did you leave? Why did you flee? And words like this. At that time it was very difficult to leave your place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it's obvious, but could you please just explain why it was -- why it was difficult to leave your place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Because the time was very difficult and it was difficult to leave your place of course. It was better to stay there and get killed than to flee. It depended on how people perceived this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could go into private session very Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. 3 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're now in private session. If -- could you please tell us, when you say "the leaders" in your previous answer, the leaders spoke to the refugees -- the villagers who had fled Grabanica, could you please tell us who those leaders are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Lahi Ibrahimaj and Alush Agushi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these two persons, do you know if they had any pseudonyms or any nicknames that they were known by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, Lahi's nickname was Magjupi and Alush's was Mala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other nicknames that Alush was known by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: That was a pseudonym that people knew them [as interpreted] by, but because he had had a surgery in his throat his voice was rather hoarse and people called him Pipi.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could go into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We're in open now. Thank you. Your Honours, I realise this is perhaps too early for the normal break, but I'm about to enter into a rather lengthy period of private session. So I'm not sure if it would be convenient to break now or if I should just begin and we can pick up after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can break now, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll resume at 25 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will be moving to another large topic, but actually one that can largely be done in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I just remind you -- I would just remind you at this point that we are in open session and please keep that in mind in your answers. And I'm going to be turning now to another topic, and I'm going to turn now to July of 1998. Was there a time -- was there a time in July 1998 when you went to Berisa? And if you could please indicate yes or no first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, could you tell us when in July of 1998 that was? Was it in the beginning or the middle or the end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was by the end of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that in the late part of July --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say at this juncture that it may well be the case that there is some dispute as to the chronology of this part of the witness's testimony. So I would ask that my friend be careful about how he phrases and captures the next few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. My silence, you understand, Mr. Shin is an acceptance of Mr. Khan's cautionary note.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I understand that. That's how I understood that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And an expectation that you will observe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I certainly will. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us, bearing in mind that we are in open session, could you tell us first, did you go there -- did you go to Berisa alone or did you go there with others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I went there with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could go briefly into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. 11 [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by later order of the Chamber]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what unit was it that you went there with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Unit 192, which was led by Commander Alush Agushi, or the leader as we called him. People also referred to it as Mala's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps it's obvious, but why was it referred to also as Mala's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Because the entire unit or most of the soldiers of that unit came from a territory where I lived -- I and Mala live or he lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. There is something unclear in the translation. It's a territory where you lived or a territory where Mala lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Both of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Should there be a redaction of the I?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We need a little bit more than the I -- oh, we're in private. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how many -- how many soldiers were in this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: 30 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long had you been with this unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know that I joined this unit in July. I participated in the fighting in Rahovec with this unit, in Rrasat e Rrahovecit. We went also together in Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, this unit, where was this unit normally based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: What time do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about at the time that you joined the unit in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I joined the unit in Malisheve because I knew them. From Malisheve we went to Rrasat e Rrahovecit. We were some members of this unit. The bulk of the unit was there and I was there then with this unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be clear, when you joined the unit, did you know where the unit was normally based? What was its normal -- where was its normal base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us where it was based? And perhaps -- perhaps you've indicated it but it may have been unclear. Was it based in Rahovec, was that your testimony, or was it based somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Those days it was based in Rrasat e Rrahovecit. At the exit of Rahovec there is a road that comes to Malisheve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could go back into open, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did somebody else you to go to Berisa? And please bear in mind we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, once again I think it's important with this witness to be quite proper about things. My friend of course knows the form of questions. He can ask the witness: Why did you go to Berisa? Rather than ask him to a particular person -- tell him. It is leading and I would ask that he exercise caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why did you go to Berisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I was -- I went there on orders by Alush Agushi, who escorted us there in order for us to assist Celiku's forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please have a redaction on the name there please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That would be Alush Agushi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there a reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could just go into private session briefly I could explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a reason, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: There is a reason, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Has that name not appeared in the transcript in open session so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I thought that it had appeared in private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Only private; very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I may be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be redacted, but you confine your application to that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you receive this order directly from the person who you said gave the order to you to assist Celiku's forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, same objection with regard to leading. I believe Mr. Shin has to ask a proper question here: Where did you receive the order? How did you receive the order? There's so many variants on how to ask the question that it would be appropriate for him to once again exercise caution here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am dubious, frankly, Mr. Guy-Smith, that this question asked in that way could be so critical, but I must agree. Technically, it is leading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, where -- where were you when you were asked to go to Berisa? Where were you located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I said even earlier, we were located at Rrasat e Rrahovecit. After we returned from that place, to Malisheve, to my recollection that day it was decided that we should go to Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please explain to us how it was you were informed you should go to Berisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If you could just clarify that. When you say "the leader," what do you mean by that? And that doesn't mean you should mention his name, but if you could just explain the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The leader of the unit where I belonged at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he come to speak to you or what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. He spoke with me and with the other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the time that you actually went to Berisa, when was it that he spoke to you and the other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: On the day when we set off for Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything else that he told you when he told you to go to Berisa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I think I mentioned it earlier as well. He told us to go and assist that unit because that territory was in jeopardy. And he sent us as a special unit when the need was for interventions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say that he told you to go and assist that unit, just so we're clear, what unit are you speaking of assisting? Or rather, what unit was he speaking of when he said you should go and assist that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: He told us to go and assist Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say that he told you to go because that territory was in jeopardy, could you explain to the Court what that means, what he explained, if he did, what that means, that the territory was in jeopardy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: In jeopardy meaning they were likely to be attacked by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you did go to -- as you said, to Berisa, where exactly did you go first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: We went to Novoselle village in the territory of Berisa, at least this is what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If with the assistance of the usher if I could please show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P001, map 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at that map and indicate when you've located where the area -- where the place where the village of Novo Selo is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Usher, if that map could please be placed on the ELMO as well. And if the witness could be given the pointer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please point to the area where Novo Selo is, the place where Novo Selo is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If the record could show, please, that the witness pointed to an area just a little to the right and a little down from the dot for Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, from what you can see on the map, is -- does the village Novo Selo, the name, does that itself appear on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, it does not appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. The map can be taken away now -- actually -- yes, you can take it away now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we have it marked in some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. fashion. A little to the right and to the left. Is going to be a bit vague if it becomes of any importance at a later point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Will you attend to that, Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Could we -- just one moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you now to look at that map again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If the usher could please place it back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at this point if the usher could give you a red pen and I'm going to ask you to look carefully at this map and even though as you indicated the name Novo Selo does not appear on this map, could you place a small circle in the area or the place where you believe Novo Selo to be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could a better marker be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is marked with a red X.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And just so we are clear, according to the map there is a road between Berisa and Klecka. And where you have drawn Novo Selo, is Novo Selo on that road, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that -- if that exhibit could be given a number, please, and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Again I ask: Why under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it does not need to be under seal; my mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P164.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you remind us again where you were -- where you were when you set off to go towards Berisa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: In Malisheve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- if you could tell us please what path you took to get to Berisa.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: From Malisheve we went in the direction of Arlat. Then we took a right turn. There was a depot then at that place. Then we passed in the direction of Terpeze and then went to Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you can recall, what time of day was it when you left from Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was day, in the afternoon I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you can recall, how long did it take you to get to Berisa, and more specifically to Novo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, could you describe -- when you say that you went to Berisa but specifically you went to -- you mentioned that you went to Novo Selo, what area does that term "Berisa," what does that describe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: From what I knew, Berisa was named for the whole territory. Novoselle, it's -- it means new village translated from the Serb word of Fshati i ri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say Berisa was named for the whole territory, could you please tell us from what you knew at that time what other villages or places are included in that territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I thought that Klecka, Divjaka, and Novoselle were part of that area from Terpeze. Up -- I thought that the place was called Berisa. This is what I think even now; I don't know how accurate I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived -- when you arrived at Novo Selo, who were you with when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The entire unit was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet anybody other than the people from your unit when you went to Berisa? If you could just indicate yes or no, please, at this point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where exactly were you when you -- when you met someone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: In that village, in Novoselle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall more specifically where in Novo Selo you were, if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly where the place was because the village is very small. It's a place from the school of Novoselle towards Divjak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about the time you met someone, could you tell us more specifically, if you can, what time of day that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact time because a lot of time had passed. I don't know if I met him that day or on the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was this person that you met?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember whether it was that day or the next day. Do you remember who you were with when you had that meeting -- when you met Commander Celiku rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question because I can't hear you very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you don't remember specifically --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I think you said that you don't remember specifically whether it was that day or the next day when you met Commander Celiku. And my question to you was: Whenever it was, whether it was that day or the next day, who were you with? And perhaps you've answered this already, but just so we're clear, who were you with when you had that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I was with my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we'll just wait for a moment while we try to fix the volume here. I think we may be okay now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what happened when -- or let me ask you this: What happened when you first -- when you met Commander Celiku, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I cannot reproduce here exactly word for word what he said, but I know that he came to meet us as a unit and he asked for a person by his pseudonym. That person -- that pseudonym was mine. I introduced myself and he addressed me with the words that for any problem that you may have -- I saw that the situation was very bad. In general he told me that, You can over come to the headquarters and ask for what you need. Since you are here and the leader for your unit for the moment is missing, you will be the person in charge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could ask you a few questions about that. First, was the leader of your unit to your knowledge at that time, was he in fact -- was he in fact missing at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: He was missing -- he was absent actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he -- when you were told that you could go to the headquarters, was there anything else that was said about the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember accurately. He might have told me to come over to the headquarter in Klecke. It was common knowledge that his headquarter was in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had told us -- you had explained to us that you introduced yourself. Now, did this person that you were speaking to, did he introduce himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: This I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then can I ask you, you say you met Commander Celiku. How is it that you knew you were meeting Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Because we were under Celiku's command. We were there to assist them. So when he came to meet was we knew that he was Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during this encounter, was -- the person you met, was he with anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any doubt in your mind that the person you were encountering at that time was indeed Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say anything during this encounter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember. We greeted each other and had a small conversation, as it's our tradition to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And perhaps it's -- it may be clear from your answers. Was this, as far as you know, the first time you were meeting this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you please describe the manner of this person that you had this encounter with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was a normal manner. I cannot single out anything specific. This is how it looked to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there at some -- a time at some point -- let me rephrase that. Did you at that time know the true identity of Commander Celiku or did you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a time later when you did learn the full name of Commander Celiku? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn that name later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember how.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that name? What was the name that you learned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you know at that time when you had that encounter, did you know whether there was an area that Commander Celiku was responsible for?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, again this is rather important. The Prosecution of course know their case. I think what the witness can be asked is what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No need to go on what the witness may be asked. You object to this particular question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will have to develop some better foundation I think, Mr. Shin, if you're going to pursue that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say that you -- your understanding at the time of this meeting was that you were meeting Commander Celiku. Did you have an understanding of what that term "commander" meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: What the word "commander" means, I knew it even earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of that term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: As a commander of a zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- if you could just answer yes or no first. Did you know at the time of that meeting whether Commander Celiku as a commander, whether he was also a commander of a zone what -- at that time of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know that? To the best of your recollection, please, and take your time if you need to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The reason I knew this was that in Dukagjini zone the commander was Ramush, while in Zatriq as was a name of a part that belonged to Rahovec was "peseqindshi" or 500. The pseudonym was so. In Drenica I knew that the commander was Sylejman Selimi or Sultani, while in a part of Lapusnik or a part of Berisa, I cannot give here the exact boundaries, I knew it was Celiku. And in Llap part, I knew it was Remi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the information you've just given the Court about these commanders and their zones, how did you learn that? Where did you learn that from to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: For the place where I was stationed I knew that for sure because I was there as part of a unit. And as time passed I knew about the other as well, but this information was transmitted and broadcast through TV and radio stations. So it was known which zone was operational and who was a commander of that specific zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say for the place where you were stationed, what area are you speaking of -- what area are you speaking of there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I'm speaking of the zone where I initially went to become a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, focusing on that time period -- first focusing on that time period when you had this encounter, what area did you think was in Celiku's zone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I mentioned this earlier. That part, that is to say Klecka, was the headquarters as I know it. It comprised some municipalities or villages that fell under certain municipalities, some villages of Malisheve municipality and some of Suhareke municipality. But I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you know -- I'm sorry, if I could rephrase that. Was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this your understanding of that zone at that time, at the time of your encounter, just so that we're clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, even before the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to ask you now a few questions about -- about your answer, a few further questions. Did you know or did you have -- what did you think was the extent to how far south that zone extended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: South from Klecka or from other location?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question was not clear. Let me try that again. Did you -- what was your -- what did you think was the southern boundary of that zone, if you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Approximately I can say that the boundary of that zone that belonged to the command of Celiku was up to the road to Pristina, the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- what did you think was the western boundary, if you know, of that zone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The western boundary I don't know exactly, but it could extend up to Malisevo or beyond Malisevo, but I don't know those villages. I'm not familiar with them. There are some villages like Carralluke and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you think at that time was the northern boundary of that zone, if you know -- if you knew at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I mentioned this earlier that the northern boundary could have been up to certain villages near Rahovec and near Suhareke, but I don't know exactly because the boundary of one command or one zone was there up to the territory that was under KLA control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, for my next question, if I could please ask the assistance of the usher to place once again -- I'm sorry, let me get the exhibit number. If I could have the last exhibit placed back -- that's Exhibit 164 placed back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if my -- Witness, I'm not sure perhaps if my question was entirely -- my last question was entirely clear. Do you -- my question was -- my question was whether -- and I used the word "northern boundary" -- sorry, the phrase "northern boundary." What I meant was looking at the top part of this map, if you could please look at the map. Looking at the upper part of this map, rather, in that direction what did you think at that time was the boundary of that zone, if you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the witness could speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could repeat exactly what you said but with the microphone closer to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I think it could have been from Arlat, the asphalt road that goes to Pristina approximately here in Komorane, but at that time Komorane was controlled by Serb forces. So I don't know the exact lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If the witness could please be given a marker to mark that line, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I caught a glimpse, Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately I'm a little hard to miss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just watch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm trying to reduce, but that's another matter. Your Honour -- Your Honour, the witness has said that he really doesn't know about the boundaries of this zone. It seems to be really another example of seeking to extract extremely unreliable, questionable evidence from a witness, and I would ask that extreme care be given, and I'm sorry I'm using that word a little too much today, but extreme care be given when a witness has said under oath that he is not sure what the boundaries of the zone are. What is the utility of seeking to get an uncertain witness to mark an uncertain piece of evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The limitations of the witness's knowledge are very clear from what he has very frankly indicated. The questioning is proceeding on the basis of no more than his then understanding based on what I would summarise as what he's heard on broadcast and radio and whatever may have been his impression as a member of the KLA in a neighbouring unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's no more than that as I understand it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I would just add what the witness said was he was not sure -- he did not know the exact lines which is something different from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, don't bother. I'm allowing you to continue so you don't need to press that on me. I'm indicating to Mr. Khan that we, too, have heard the limitations of his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, my mistake for underestimating Your Honours on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I doubt it. The witness has pointed to the main asphalt road as his understanding in this area and as far as Komorane. Is there really much point in marking that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Usher, there will be no need to give the witness the pen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
