utterances.text: Witness, did you have any knowledge at that time about persons who may have been -- I'm sorry. Let me rephrase that. Did you know at that time who - and I mean at the time of that encounter - who were persons under the command of Commander Celiku? Just yes or no, please, first.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, not on the day I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had told us earlier that you had been ordered to go to this area because of some activity by the Serbian forces. Did I understand you correctly there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time of your meeting with Commander Celiku, did you have any further information at that time about this activity of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm not trying to be difficult, but for the record the record should be clear. The witness has not talked about Serbian activity. He did talk about jeopardy, and it's quite a different thing. It may be one and the same, but I think that's of course for the witness to say and not of course for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have to confess having a slightly more vivid imagination than you, Mr. Khan. I had no doubt if this unit was in jeopardy, there was one source of the jeopardy. But I think it will come a little clearer in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if it may be of assistance to my learned colleague, on line 4 -- page 32, line 4, perhaps there will be some explanation -- he can find what he's looking for there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry about that. My question was: At the time of your meeting with Commander Celiku, did you have any further information at that time about the activity of the Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was a time when the Serb forces attacked several points that were controlled by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "it was a time," when you tell us that, do you mean that the Serb forces were attacking several points controlled by the KLA on that day, on that day that you met Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: On that day as well there were attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, did you know that there were these attacks on that day itself or did you learn this later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: When I left Rrasat e Rrahovecit there were attacks, but other units assumed positions there. The major part of the unit been there for several days then. I left that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could ask the question this way going back to your answer that: "It was a time when the Serb forces attacked several points that were controlled by the KLA." Could you please tell us what points you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: For example, the Lapusnik gorge was attacked and Rrasat e Rrahovecit as well so that they could penetrate the zones controlled by the KLA. And there was also penetration from the part of Kijeve that was under Serb control in the direction of Malisheve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that the Lapusnik gorge was attacked. Can I ask you first, if you know, does the Lapusnik gorge, does that include Lapusnik village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, I think it includes the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the time of your encounter with Commander Celiku, when was the Lapusnik gorge attacked as far as you can know, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm trying to be clear. I don't know. But the day we went the attack could have happened earlier but what I know was that it was either on that day or the next day that the Lapusnik gorge was overtaken by the Serbs, the Lapusnik gorge fell in the hands of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, returning to your encounter with Commander Celiku, could you tell us how did that -- how did that encounter end?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: After that brief conversation - I can't tell you how long it lasted - we settled in that village. We accommodated ourselves in three rooms. Celiku went, he left. There was a point at Novoselle school. That was where we changed our shifts. Now and again we surveyed the terrain. We went to Terpeze village sometimes where there were concentrations of Serb -- of KLA forces, sorry. There were -- there was shelling. The Serb forces had shelled the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'd just ask you one question about that. You say that when Celiku left, did you see how he left? Did you see how he -- well, how he left your encounter, by what means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: He left by car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet -- let me ask you this: Could you please describe Commander Celiku when you met him on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: He was dressed in uniform. He was of average height. He had a beard, not a very large beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Did you meet Commander Celiku again? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And taking it step by step, let me ask you first: When in relation to this first meeting with Commander Celiku, when did this other meeting or this next meeting take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly when. A few days after that. I can't tell you exactly how many days after. Maybe three or four days, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this next meeting - again taking it step by step - could you tell the Court how this meeting came about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Before going to meet Celiku I was on a hill near Terpeze village with some other soldiers. One of the soldiers called me by my pseudonym. He said, Someone wants you. We walked for a while from the place we were located. We went to the road. There was a bearded soldier. When we went to the car it was a Golf 3, dark red. There I saw Qerqizi. Then I -- then I learned that he was Qerqizi. We got in the car. I don't know that part of the -- of the country very well, but I know that we went to Klecka. And it was there that I met with Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I could interrupt you at that point to ask you a few questions. You say that you saw Qerqizi and that you learned that he was --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you learned -- and that you learned that he was Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself as Qerqizi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then how did you know that that was Qerqizi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: When we went to Klecka to the headquarter, then I heard people calling him by that name, by a pseudonym. I had a short conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you in a minute about that conversation. At that time when you heard people calling him by his pseudonym when you were at Klecka at the headquarters -- or when you were at Klecka, did you know -- did you know Qerqizi's full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Qerqizi's full name at some point later in time? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, it was much later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us first of all approximately when to the best of your recollection it was that you learned Qerqizi's full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: It was after the war of course, but I can't tell you when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, can you remember how it is that you learned his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember. It is possible that through the media, but I know that it was a long time after the war that I found that out or maybe when it became public that Qerqizi's name was what it was or maybe when I heard the indictment. I don't know. It was much later. When I was in the war, I knew him as Qerqizi only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you know -- when you did learn, what did you know his full name to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Maybe, as I said, when I saw the name in the media that he was a leader and then he was accused by the ICTY and then they published his full name along with the pseudonym. And then I connected the fact that I knew the pseudonym to the name. This is all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I was unclear about my question. What did you learn -- what did you learn was his true name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to go back a little to an answer you gave earlier to ask some questions -- to ask some further questions. You said that you were on a hill near Terpeze village when a soldier came to you and said someone wants you. Did you learn -- did you learn who that someone was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No, I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question was probably unclear. Did you learn who it was that wanted you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: To my recollection after we got into the car they told me that Celiku wants to talk to you. We talked about some ordinary matters, as I said earlier, just courtesy talk about problems we had and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, if I could just ask you some questions to take this step by step. You told us that you saw Qerqizi at the car. And now you've told us you've gotten into that car. Who went into that car with you? If you could please tell us all the persons in that car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Qerqizi that I remembered and saw again in the headquarter in Klecke, that's why I memorised him, as well as another person I don't remember. I don't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in total there were -- there were three in that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you in fact arrive in Klecka in that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, taking this step by step, where specifically in Klecka did you go first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The headquarter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, could you please describe the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I can, approximately. On the road to the -- to Klecka from Novoselle you climb. There is a long -- you climb the road. There is a long wall on the left. There is a small hill, again on the left. You enter the courtyard. There were big doors. Then again on the left there was a building where we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you went to this building, was it just you or was it the other occupants of that car as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: No. They -- those persons as well, but there were other persons there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you had some discussions in the car about problems that you had and other matters. Were there any further discussions after you arrived at this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please, because the voice comes very loud to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I could have the assistance of the usher. We may have overcompensated on the volume last time. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm grateful for the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, is that a comfortable volume for you now? If --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, it's okay now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... with the volume at some point, please don't hesitate to mention that. My question was this: You have told us that in the car with Qerqizi and this other person you had some discussions on the way to Klecka, including discussions about problems that you had and some other matters. Did this discussion -- did you have further discussions with the occupants of the car after you arrived in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, first of all, who did you have those discussions with? Who was present during them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: There were many people present there. There was one -- someone by the pseudonym of Gazetari. There was someone who had the same last name as me. I don't know who he was. I don't remember. It was Qerqizi and the same person with whom I came in the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could just out of an abundance of caution redact the phrase "someone with the same last name as me." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I may have been unclear in my question. We will get to your discussions with these other persons, but before that did you have any discussions with -- any further discussions once you got to Klecka with the persons who were in the car with you or with a person in the car with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes, we had a discussion about a problem of some girls; they were sisters from Terpeze. I don't know how the conversation started, actually, who was the first to start that topic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry, if I could interrupt you. And I'm sorry to take this in such a piecemeal, step-by-step fashion but I have to. If I could ask you first, who did you have this discussion with, just so we're clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: With the two persons I travelled in the car after we entered the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else present when -- in your conversation with these two other persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were other persons who were part of the conversation or persons who could hear the conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: They were not part of the conversation. They only could hear if they were interested, but they talked about other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, I apologise for interrupting you. If you could now continue. You were describing the conversation and you were saying that you don't know how the conversation started or who was the first to start that topic. And if you could please pick up from there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: So the conversation was about these girls, and as I said I told them that there was -- there had been a problem with them, that they were questioned. They were accused of being Serb spies and of being in relationships with Serbs. The persons who I was discussing this with, so we were three persons, they told me that it wasn't a problem for me to deal with and that I should look after my unit. And my answer was that I'm there and I want to know what's going on, but we did not continue with this conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness, I'm going to ask you a few questions about that, but maybe I can ask you first, can you -- did you have -- were all three of you talking or was it just two of you? Who was actually -- who was it who said -- who told you that it wasn't a problem for you to deal with? What was that who said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I more or less tried to explain this conversation and the meaning of this conversation. Now I cannot tell exactly who told me what because this was a brief conversation with these persons. This wasn't a person -- a problem that I was dealing with seriously, so we just left it there and we didn't proceed with the conversation. So I cannot tell you for sure who told me what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said that someone, one of these two other persons I take it, told you that it wasn't a problem for you to deal with, can you explain what they meant by that as far as you understood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I really don't know how to explain this further. Simply, it's not a problem. It's not your business. It's not a big problem for you to be interested in. Something like this. And we ended this conversation and it was very short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how long was that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know precisely, but it was brief, very brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that conversation ended, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: After this conversation another person, I don't know him, he told us to enter another room or an office. So if you look at it from the room where we were, it was on the right side, this other room. We entered it, and there we discussed the problems and the situation with the units at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, I'm going to take this step by step as well. Can you first describe the room that you entered, physically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: The first room that we went to, I know that near the door there was a TV, there was some cables. I know that the room was in wood. The room to the right had more or less -- was also laid in wood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could ask you next, was there anyone -- when you entered that room, was there anyone in that room already, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: So when we entered the room on the right as you enter there was Celiku seated. There were several other persons who I don't know. One of them was the person responsible for a unit, Guri. I knew him from before. I greeted him. There I also saw the person with a pseudonym I mentioned earlier, Gazetari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could ask you next, you say that "we entered the room." How many of you entered the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately how many, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Approximately we were ten in that room; some were already there, some came later. I know when after we entered we began a conversation. Another leader of a unit came in; I knew him as Kumanova. And he spoke very briefly in a shape of a report and he left the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could take the -- what happened in that room step by step. Who was the first person who spoke in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly and I'm not able to say the -- that this and this person spoke because we were all members of units. To put it shortly, we were all Albanians and we speak not like here in this courtroom but we have like free conversations and jokes. I know that Celiku asked everyone to speak of the problems, but this does not mean that he took the floor first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Celiku asked everyone to speak of the problems. Did people -- did people respond? And if you could tell us first of all -- I'm sorry. I'll leave the question there. Did people respond to his request, did the people in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: Yes. I know that when the leader of Guri unit described the problems with his unit and others did so, I was not requested to give a report for my unit because my unit was stationed in -- that was then in Berisa was stationed in another place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that Celiku asked people to speak of problems. Was there anyone else in that room who requested people to speak of problems or other issues, or was that only Celiku?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SHEFQET KABASHI
utterances.text: To my knowledge, only Celiku.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, we're getting to the point of the tape where we must finish. I don't want to cut in at a critical point of what you're doing, but when you see a convenient moment in the near future we will stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I think I will only be about five more minutes here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that may be too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Oh, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if my learned friend would consider as one of his last questions in the three minutes available to invite the witness to indicate whether it is said that my client was in this room. I raise that because we have no prior notice of any of this evidence. It doesn't appear in any statement that I have seen, so we're hearing this for the very first time. So I would be grateful for any assistance to enable me to take any instructions as to whether it is being said that my client is here at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I would respectfully second that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you've had your answer already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, my point is different, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have had no notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: This is evidence we are hearing for the first time today. It does not appear in any Prosecution disclosure, at least the disclosure I've got, the two statements. The details of this meeting have not been provided to us or at least I haven't got them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Shin -- you, too, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is on somewhat of a different matter. If there have any corrections or explanations in any statements that have been previously discussed with the witness is what Mr. Shin raised at the very beginning of his examination of this witness at page 5, line 5, I was planning on objecting with regard to the issue of whether a witness can render an opinion on their own truthfulness, but that's a secondary matter. It says: "Apart from some corrections and explanations which we had discussed earlier this week, were you as truthful as you could be in these statements?" We've received no, as they have been I would euphemistically call, proofing notes, or as it has been called supplemental information sheets which indicate there has been any corrections or explanations, or what those corrections or explanations would have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, are you able to answer Mr. Topolski's question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, in fact I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is the answer yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It appears to me from what I've heard from three counsel that there may be need over the weekend for some indication to the Defence of the evidence that is to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, we did a supplemental disclosure on the 8th of March, 2005, which I have a copy of. I'm not quite sure what has happened if they have not in fact received a copy of this. This is a matter that we may be able to clarify but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it has been said that two of the counsel, counsel for two accused have had no notice of this part of the evidence at least at all. The third has had no clarification or modification. I don't want to go into the detail of who's had what, but the Chamber expects counsel to resolve now when we adjourn the situation so that there is due notice to the Defence of any material evidence affecting their respective clients that is anticipated from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. We have provided this information and I will find -- look into what has happened in the transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to take time but just as a matter of fairness it does appear that one of our number does have the supplemental information. It may be our fault that it wasn't distributed. But, Your Honour, we'll look over it over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A bit of tidying up needed in one or both camps and we will leave you to it. Witness, we must adjourn now for the weekend and your evidence will continue on Monday at 2.15 or as soon after that as the courtroom becomes available. I'm told there is to be interspersed between the morning and afternoon an initial appearance and it may mean that we are a few moments late in starting. We will adjourn now until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
